name: Data Converter
description: Convert anything in one DBX workbench panel: 13 formats (JSON / YAML / XML / Properties / TOML / INI / .env / CSV / TSV / Query / Headers / Cookie / HTML) in any combination, JSONPath / jq queries with JSON Schema validation, eight escape tools (URL / Base64 / HTML / JSON / Unicode / Hex / SQL / Regex), batch text to SQL (IN / NOT IN / INSERT), .xlsx / .csv / .tsv to JSON, Image ⇄ Base64, and a Byte Converter (B/KB/MB/GB/TB/PB on both the 1000 and 1024 scales, exact ⇄ human readable, batch totals, plus hex dump / byte array / binary string). A Time Converter turns timestamps and dates into each other (local, T-separated, UTC, ISO 8601 and relative) one value per line, with foldable results and copies that carry results only. A Code Gen page turns a JSON sample or a CREATE TABLE into TypeScript / Go / Java / Python models, and a Chart page renders an ECharts option (or bare numbers) as a real chart, 700 x 400 by default with custom width and height, exported as PNG or SVG, and a QR code page turns any text into a batch of codes (size, error correction, margin and colours adjustable, an icon in the middle, PNG or SVG export) or decodes pictures back into text. The navigation bar is yours to arrange: drag the eleven entries into your own order, pin the ones you use most (they are the last to fall into More when the window narrows), and keep the bar sticky; the setup is remembered along with the layout. Pure frontend, no backend, works offline.

versions.releaseNotes: Initial release with multi-format conversion, mock data generation, and i18n support.

0.1.5 (update): a new Byte Converter page converts B / KB / MB / GB / TB / PB on the 1000 and 1024 scales side by side (1234567890 → 1.23 GB and 1.15 GiB), goes back from a human-readable value to an exact byte count, handles batches of sizes with a running total, and turns byte sequences (1f 8b 08, [0x1f, 0x8b], binary, xxd dumps) into hex dump / byte array / binary string. The Convert page now handles 13 formats in any source/target combination — TOML, INI, .env, CSV, TSV, query strings, HTTP headers, cookie strings and HTML tables join JSON / YAML / XML / Properties. A Query page runs JSONPath and jq-style expressions and validates against a JSON Schema draft-07 subset, an Escaping page converts both ways between URL / Base64 / HTML / JSON string / \uXXXX / hex / SQL / regex, and Code Gen turns JSON or CREATE TABLE into TypeScript / Go / Java / Python models. All nine pages are translated into 14 languages, and everything runs locally: no network, no eval, with hard limits on size, rows and columns.

Every page can now import a file — the page you are on handles it, and the size limit is shown on the drop overlay before you release. The Chart page also digs charts out of real backend exports: a task list whose payload is itself serialized JSON, business keys six layers deep with thousands of table rows in between. Charts that used to be missed are now listed in a Chart picker by title, and the status line says so when an input is too large to scan completely. Charts are always drawn on the light palette with a white background, so a dark theme no longer changes the image you export.
0.1.6 (update): a new Chart page renders an ECharts option — or just an array of numbers — as a real chart, 700 x 400 by default with an editable width and height, exported as PNG at 1x / 2x / 3x or as vector SVG; the ECharts 6.1.0 engine ships inside the package, loads only when you open the page and works inside the DBX sandbox. The Image ⇄ Base64 page gained file import, so everything it exports can be imported back. Every save now reports what actually happened (saved, downloaded, cancelled or failed) instead of always claiming success. All ten pages are translated into 14 languages, and everything runs locally: no network, no eval.

A new Time Converter page turns timestamps and dates into each other. Paste one value per line — 2020-01-01, 2020-01-01 00:00:00, 2020-01-01T00:00:00, 1577836800 or 1577836800000 — and every line is converted into the notations you enable. Five shortcut buttons — Now, Today start, Yesterday, Week start and Month start — append the matching moment as a new line in one click, truncated to the second. Seven toggles cover Unix seconds, Unix milliseconds, local time, local time with T, UTC, ISO 8601 and relative time; local and local-with-T are on by default, so the everyday 2020-01-01 00:00:00 <-> 2020-01-01T00:00:00 swap works out of the box. Results come as one card per line: the header folds it away, moving the caret to line N highlights card N, every value copies on click, and the Copy button writes results only — one output line per input line, fields joined by spaces, no index, no original value, no labels. Relative time stays for reading and never enters the copy. A batch caps at 2000 lines and a bad line is flagged on its own. All eleven pages are translated into 14 languages, and everything runs locally: no network, no eval.

Your navigation bar now fits the way you work: a sliders button in the top bar opens Navigation settings, where the eleven entries can be dragged (or nudged with arrows) into any order and the ones you reach for most can be pinned — pinned entries stay in front and are the last to fall into the More menu when the window narrows. Sticky navigation bar keeps the bar at the top while content scrolls, and in the left-hand column pinned entries stay glued to the top as the column scrolls. Everything is remembered across reloads and restarts through the host plugin storage, stored under its own versioned key so rolling back to an older build is safe and upgrading again keeps your setup; new entries are appended to the end automatically, no migration needed. Also fixed: the More menu no longer scrambles pinned and unpinned entries together, and dragging a row now works inside the workbench, where the host webview takes over native drag and drop — reordering runs on pointer events instead. Generate QR codes in batches, or read them back out of pictures. One line becomes one code — a column of links, ids or any short text turns into a wall of codes; switch the split to whole block and the line breaks stay inside a single code. Size, error correction, margin, foreground and background colours are all settings, and an icon can sit in the middle (uploading one pushes the error correction to H, the only level at which a code with a hole in the middle still decodes). Cards fold down to their number plus a preview, jump the cursor back to the line they came from, copy their own text or image, and a single export opens a small panel where format, size and file name are settled on the spot — the choice is remembered for the next card; double-clicking a code opens it full screen in a lightbox that stays sharp at any zoom; the whole batch exports as a single tiled PNG. The second tab decodes dropped images, pasted screenshots or a batch of files into text, line breaks included. Both engines ship offline and load as blob: URLs, and text is encoded as UTF-8, so Chinese content decodes correctly. Your navigation can now live on the left. A layout button at the far right of the top bar moves the eleven navigation entries into a vertical column (13rem wide) and hands the content area the same space back; click again to return to the top, which stays the default. On the left the top bar keeps only the brand, the language switcher and this button; the format-convert picker moves to the top of the column and expands inside it, pushing the entries down instead of floating over them. The vertical column fits every entry, so "More" no longer appears. Your choice is remembered across reloads and app restarts through the host plugin storage (the workbench sandbox has an opaque origin, so localStorage is not available there); when the host cannot store it, the plugin falls back to browser localStorage and then to window.name, which is the only channel that survives inside the dbx-plugin dev sandbox (localStorage, sessionStorage and cookies all throw there). A small fix rides along: navigation entries and the gaps between them are tighter, so all eleven still fit a 1440-wide window now that the button and the eleventh entry are there. All twelve pages stay translated into 14 languages, and everything still runs locally: no network, no eval.

zh-CN.name: 数据转换
zh-CN.description: 在 DBX 工作台里一次转完：JSON / YAML / XML / Properties / TOML / INI / .env / CSV / TSV / Query / Headers / Cookie / HTML 共 13 种格式任意互转、JSONPath / jq 查询与 JSON Schema 校验（含从样例反推 Schema）、URL / Base64 / HTML / JSON / Unicode / Hex / SQL / 正则 8 种转义互转、字节换算（B / KB / MB / GB / TB / PB，1000 与 1024 两套进制，精确值 ⇄ 人类可读，批量求和，以及 hex dump / 字节数组 / 二进制串）、批量文本生成 SQL（IN / NOT IN / INSERT）、.xlsx / .csv / .tsv 转 JSON，以及图片 ↔ Base64；「代码生成」页把一段 JSON 示例或一条 CREATE TABLE 直接变成 TypeScript / Go / Java / Python 模型；「JSON 转图表」页把一段 ECharts option（或一组数字）直接画成图，默认 700 × 400、宽高可改，可导出 PNG / SVG；「时间转换」页把时间戳与日期批量互转（本地时间 / `T` 分隔 / UTC / ISO 8601 / 相对时间任选，结果可折叠、可单个复制）；「二维码转换」页把一段文本批量生成二维码（尺寸 / 纠错 / 边距 / 配色可调，中心可放图标，导出 PNG / SVG），也能把图片里的二维码解回文本。导航栏可以自己排：拖动调整十一个入口的顺序、把常用项置顶（窗口变窄时最后才被收进「更多」）、导航条吸顶，设置连同布局一起记住。纯前端、无后端、可离线运行。

zh-TW.name: 資料轉換
